Base outfit: several days (five access bosses with a 20 h cooldown and the final boss with 68 h). Addons: minutes if you buy both items on the Market; many attempts if you hunt them yourself

The {wiki:Revenant Outfits|Revenant Outfits} are the reward of the {wiki:Soul War Quest|Soul War Quest}: you receive the base outfit when you defeat {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} and report the task to the {npc:Flickering Soul}, in {wiki:Zarganash}. The first addon is obtained by using {item:The Skull of a Beast}, which drops from four of the Soul War access bosses; the second by using a {item:Bracelet of Strengthening}, which drops from {creature:Goshnar's Hatred}. Both items can also be bought on the Market. With both addons you earn the achievement **Unleash the Beast**.
Help Goshnar defeat the manifestation of his evil traits and earn the right to wear the Revenant Outfits.
Flickering Soul, in the Soul War hub in Zarganash
Level **250** (**700+** recommended for the outfits; the wiki states *600?* for the Soul War Quest).
**Base outfit:** complete the {wiki:Soul War Quest|Soul War Quest}, defeating {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} and reporting the {key:task} to the {npc:Flickering Soul}.
For the Soul War Quest: have completed the {wiki:Feaster of Souls Quest|Feaster of Souls Quest} (it is the one that gives access to Zarganash).
To travel to {wiki:Vengoth} with {npc:Harlow}: have reached at least mission 4 (*The Dark Lands*) of the {wiki:The Blood Brothers Quest|Blood Brothers Quest}.
Team: all bosses, including the final one, allow **up to 5 players**. The usual composition is a blocking **Knight** and four shooters (Paladin, Sorcerer and Druids).
**Addon 1:** use {item:The Skull of a Beast}. **Addon 2:** use a {item:Bracelet of Strengthening}. Both items drop from the Soul War bosses or can be bought on the Market.
addon 1; dropped by Goshnar's Malice, Greed, Spite or Cruelty, or bought on the Market
addon 2; dropped by Goshnar's Hatred, or bought on the Market
to cancel the monster teleport from the 1st taint and help push summons
against fear in Ebb and Flow and at Goshnar's Spite, and to generate Pulsating Energies in the Furious Crater
preferred area rune at Goshnar's Megalomania
150 gp for {npc:Harlow}'s boat (100 gp to Vengoth and 50 gp to return to Yalahar), plus the boat to Yalahar
Plenty of potions and elemental protection suited to each area (see each section)
Base {wiki:Revenant Outfits|Revenant Outfit} (male and female), when you report to the {npc:Flickering Soul} after defeating Goshnar's Megalomania
Addon 1, when you use {item:The Skull of a Beast}
Addon 2, when you use the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening}
Achievement **Unleash the Beast** (8 points), when you have both addons

Base: when you report the {key:task} to the {npc:Flickering Soul} after defeating {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania}. Addons: by using {item:The Skull of a Beast} and the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening}.
Requires Premium. Both addon items can be bought on the Market.

{item:The Skull of a Beast} and the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} are **tradeable** (Market) and no NPC buys or sells them. If you don't want to hunt the bosses, buy them from other players: the effect is the same. The base outfit, however, always requires the completed Soul War Quest.

The five access bosses have a **20-hour** cooldown each and the final boss **68 hours** (2 days and 20 hours). According to the boss pages, Malice, Greed, Spite, Cruelty and Megalomania give you at most **20 minutes** of fighting. Each time you want to kill the final boss you have to kill the five access bosses again, so each full cycle gives you several chances at the addon items as loot.
The progress of each access **is lost if you leave the zone**: you have to repeat the access to reach the boss again. Bring everything you need before going in.

All players, especially the shooters, should wear {item:Stone Skin Amulet|Stone Skin Amulets} and {item:Might Ring|Might Rings} throughout the fight: {creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters} appear in every boss room and deal very strong critical hits.
Each boss's mechanics are essential: if you fail them, the boss gets stronger. For weaker teams, failing twice can be enough to make the boss impossible to kill in time.

Keep the summons on the Knight (luring) and don't let the shooters take melee hits. With the taints, Dreadful Harvesters appear and teleport all the time: each player's position and movement count as one more mechanic.
1. Reaching Zarganash and accepting the task

The base outfit is the final reward of the {wiki:Soul War Quest|Soul War Quest}. Here you have the route and a summary of each part. These steps also serve for hunting the addon items, because both drop from the Soul War access bosses.

Take a boat to **Yalahar**: in **Thais** talk to {npc:Captain Bluebear} ({key:hi}, {key:yalahar}, {key:yes}, 200 gp) or in **Liberty Bay** to {npc:Jack Fate} ({key:hi}, {key:yalahar}, {key:yes}, 275 gp). In Liberty Bay, {npc:Captain Max} (east boat) also takes you for 400 gp, but only after you have started the {wiki:In Service of Yalahar Quest|In Service of Yalahar Quest}. You disembark at Yalahar harbour.
Captain Max, Liberty Bay east boat

Go to the docks of Yalahar's **Trade Quarter** (straight **south** from the main gate) and talk to {npc:Harlow}: {key:hi}, {key:vengoth}, {key:yes} (100 gp). He drops you off in the **west** of {wiki:Vengoth}.
Harlow only takes you if you have already reached mission 4 (*The Dark Lands*) of the Blood Brothers Quest.

In Vengoth, walk **north-east** to the **invisible** teleport to {wiki:Zarganash}, at the coordinate point, and step into it. Access to Zarganash is obtained in the {wiki:Feaster of Souls Quest|Feaster of Souls Quest}, and the Soul War requires that quest to be completed.

Inside Zarganash, cross the dungeon to the **far south-west** and enter the teleport there. You arrive at a teleport hub: it is the base of the whole Soul War Quest, with the {npc:Flickering Soul} and the {wiki:Fog Portal|Fog Portals} to the five zones.
Teleport to the Soul War hub (south-west of Zarganash)
In the hub, talk to the {npc:Flickering Soul} (it is Goshnar's soul): say {key:hi}, {key:task} and {key:yes}. From here on you have to destroy Goshnar's *fettered vices*, one boss in each zone.

Each access boss you kill gives you a {wiki:Goshnar's Taints|Goshnar's Taint} (penalty), **always in the same order**, whichever boss it is. Killing the same boss again does not give a new taint. Taints only work inside the Soul War zones (including the boss rooms) and you can see yours in the status bar. To find out which bosses you already have a taint from, say {key:shards} to the {npc:Flickering Soul}.
10% chance of a monster teleporting next to you (2 seconds before, a warning effect appears on the monster and on you; a {item:Magic Wall Rune} on the square where you were cancels the teleport)
0.5% chance of a new monster spawning near you when you hit another one
10% chance of a monster fully healing instead of dying
You lose 10% of your current health and mana every 10 seconds (applies in the final fight)

If someone dies in a fight but has dealt damage to the boss, they still receive the taint, as long as the rest of the team kills the boss. You can clear your taints by saying {key:penalties} or {key:taints} to the Flickering Soul, but after gaining or losing taints you have to wait **two weeks** to do so.
The Fog Portals and the recommended order

You can kill the bosses in any order, but the most common one (given the difficulty of the accesses and the bosses) is the one in the table. The Fog Portals stand side by side in the hub; the “Portal” column counts them from left to right. The final boss is in the portal to the **south-west** of the hub.
Collect 40, 55 and 70 {item:Pulsating Energy|Pulsating Energies} on three floors
Have killed the five access bosses
Soul War hub: each zone's portal and boss
Recommended protection: **Death** and **Fire**. Attack with **Ice**. {creature:Goshnar's Malice} can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1).
In the hub, enter the **first Fog Portal on the left**. You arrive at a safe zone. From here on you have to survive **three raids in a row**, each in an enclosed area and lasting **2 minutes**.

Enter the raid area **all together**: the first player to walk past the {item:Sandtimer} at the entrance starts the timer, and a few seconds later a wall appears that closes off the entrance. Right after that, waves of {creature:Brachiodemon|Brachiodemons} and {creature:Infernal Phantom|Infernal Phantoms} start spawning. Hold out for **2 minutes**: at the end the monsters disappear and the team is teleported to the next area. The recommended strategy is to run to a corner, with the shooters against the walls and the Knight a few steps into the spawn, so that the monsters attack him when they spawn.

After each raid you are teleported next to a {item:Magic Forcefield|teleport}: that is the **exit**. To continue, always go down the nearby **stairs**. {creature:Infernal Demon|Infernal Demons} always attack the player with the **lowest maximum health**: plan your positions with that in mind.

The most common cause of failure is not killing the monsters quickly enough: the ones left over turn on the shooters. Constant damage is what matters most. After leaving a raid area, you have to wait **3 minutes** before you can enter it again.
After the third raid, the team is sent to a room with a Fog Portal that leads to the lever room of {creature:Goshnar's Malice}. Go in and get ready (up to 5 players).

The boss **reflects 100% of the damage** it takes and **heals itself** when it hits you, so avoid its spells. The blocker has to hold all the creatures: the boss, two {creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters} and two {creature:Malicious Soul|Malicious Souls} (some only appear a few seconds later). The Knight should use {spell:Challenge} whenever possible (the boss and the summons switch targets often) and avoid standing in front of the boss. Wear protection against **Death** (and the Knight against **Ice** too, because of the boss's wave and beam).

A {wiki:Soul Cage} appears in the **north** part of the room. All the shooters kill it in under **14 seconds**; if not, the boss absorbs it and gets stronger (it takes less damage, deals more and the reflection rises from 100% to around 200%). Keep the boss away from the Soul Cage, or it heals itself and the summons for 14,000–20,000 HP.

{item:White Stone Tile|White tiles} appear around the room (never in the same spots). Stand on one: 3 seconds later all the other squares take 7,000–9,000 Death. Alternatively, take the hit with a Stone Skin Amulet, a Might Ring and at least one piece with {wiki:Powerful Lich Shroud} (around 1,000–1,200 damage).
Anyone attacking with Physical or Death damage loses **two charges** of Stone Skin per turn because of the reflection: keep an eye on your charges and swap amulets in time.

Alternative strategy: the Knight stands against a wall, completely surrounded by the boss and the 4 summons. It only works if the boss is guaranteed to stay **diagonal** (otherwise the Knight takes all the waves and heals the boss through Life Leech) and it requires close attention to the white tiles.

Open the boss's corpse. Among Crystal Coins, potions and gems, it can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1). The wiki's statistics also record a {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} (addon 2) in its loot (5.9% in a sample of only 17 kills). If it is the first time you kill this boss, you get a taint (the 1st, in the recommended order).
75,000 experience; possible The Skull of a Beast or Bracelet of Strengthening

The wiki does not describe the exit from the boss room: go back the way you came. The only exit the wiki mentions in this zone is the {item:Magic Forcefield|teleport} next to the spot where you are dropped at the end of each raid; use it (or the safe zone at the entrance) to return to the Flickering Soul's hub. Remember that if you leave the Claustrophobic Inferno, you lose your access progress.
Recommended protection: **Holy** and **Ice**. Attack with **Fire**. {creature:Goshnar's Greed} can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1; 2.0% in a sample of 49 kills).
In the hub, enter the **rightmost** Fog Portal. You arrive at a safe zone.
Map of the Mirrored Nightmare, with the temple portal that leads to the boss

To enter the boss room you have to kill **25** of each: {creature:Druid's Apparition}, {creature:Knight's Apparition}, {creature:Monk's Apparition}, {creature:Paladin's Apparition} and {creature:Sorcerer's Apparition}. The apparitions appear when you attack a {wiki:Mirror Image}: it is most likely to turn into the apparition of the vocation of whoever attacked it first, but any other one can come out. Balance the kills so you don't waste time. There are more Mirror Images on the **underground** floor of the map, but there is less room there and it is more dangerous.
With the 125 kills done, go to the **temple portal** (marked on the map in the step “Entering the Mirrored Nightmare”) and enter the room of {creature:Goshnar's Greed}.

At the start the boss is **immune to all damage**. The Knight blocks it in the **north** of the room and can run from right to left to take less damage (and stop the boss healing through Life Leech), while the shooters handle the mechanics.

A {creature:Greedbeast} spawns in the centre-left of the room. Kill it quickly (Sudden Death Runes or waves): only after **5 Greedbeasts** have died does the boss become vulnerable. Those killed while the boss is vulnerable **do not count**. It deals a lot of Life Drain: usually a Paladin with a {item:Necklace of the Deep} blocks it.

The boss is stuck in the **north-west** and vulnerable for **40 seconds**. A {creature:Soul Sphere} appears in the **north-east** and slowly walks towards it: if it gets there, it **fully heals the boss**. One shooter kills the sphere; the others deal all the damage they can to the boss.

Two {creature:Weak Soul|Weak Souls} (left and right) and a {creature:Soulsnatcher} (south) appear. Lead them onto an active {item:Active Spirit Vortex|blue vortex} to make them disappear. The vortices alternate between active (15 seconds) and {item:Inactive Vortex|inactive crystal} (25 seconds). A Weak Soul becomes a {creature:Strong Soul} after 8 seconds, a {creature:Powerful Soul} after another 8 and, 8 seconds later, disappears and strengthens the boss.

To save time, during the vulnerable phase leave the Greedbeast that spawns on low health and only kill it when the boss becomes immune again: it then counts straight away as the first of the next 5. Many teams put the 4 shooters in a line across the middle of the room: one at the far left, the Paladin on top of the Greedbeast spawn, another in the centre for the Soulsnatcher and the last one at the far right. {item:Magic Wall Rune|Magic Walls} and {item:Wild Growth Rune|Wild Growths} help push the Weak Souls into the corner vortices.
Open the boss's corpse: it can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1).
150,000 experience; possible The Skull of a Beast
The wiki does not describe the exit from the boss room: go back the way you came to the Flickering Soul's hub.

Recommended protection: **Earth** and **Ice** (at the boss: **Death**, **Earth** and **Energy**). Attack with **Fire** (at the boss also **Death**). {creature:Goshnar's Spite} can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1).

In the hub, enter the **middle** Fog Portal. You arrive at a safe zone. To reach the boss you have to kill **20 {creature:Hazardous Phantom|Hazardous Phantoms}**, but the map alternates between **flooded** and **dry** every **2 minutes**.
The monsters here cause fear (*Feared*): first a ghostly smoke effect appears and, 2 seconds later, a blue ghost applies the fear to one of the characters.

Use a 2-minute timer: it is hard to spot the clues in the middle of the fight. The small puddles on the ground go from small to medium **80 seconds** after it dries out, which means there are **40 seconds** left before it floods again.

On the rooftops, you move from building to building via the rafts. You cannot go down the ramps. If you fall into a hole you end up on the floor below (inside the building) and **there is no way to get back up** or to leave through the doors. If you are on a raft when the water goes down, you fall to the floor below (outside the buildings).

You walk freely on the lower floor, open doors, enter the buildings and use the ramps, but you cannot use the rafts between rooftops. If the water rises and you are not on a raft, you are teleported to the entrance (safe zone); if you are on a raft, you go to the roof of the nearest building.
The puddles that show how long is left until the water comes back
Since September 2022 it is **no longer** possible to use {spell:Levitate} from the lower floor onto the rafts. Older guides or videos that suggest it are out of date.

Most common strategy: wait for the last **20–30 seconds** before the water rises and run together to the **south-east** raft. If someone gets stuck or is pushed away by the fear, they only have to hold out a few seconds until the water rises and teleports them to the safe zone. On the raft, lay {item:Fire Bomb Rune|Fire Bombs} and stand on them so you aren't pushed away by the fear, and hold the position. When the water rises, you end up in the building to the **west** of the raft: stay in a corner and throw Fire Bombs around you so you aren't pushed into holes or onto other rafts.

Strong teams can run as soon as the water goes down and clear the monsters before the south-east raft ({coord:33945,31098,9}). Only if they can handle the whole area (more than a full box on the Knight), but they gain time to recover mana before the water rises.

In the southern building, keep killing the monsters that spawn around you, including a {creature:Hazardous Phantom}, until you reach the **20**. They can take a few minutes to spawn: it is the longest access of the quest and can easily take over **an hour**. Stronger teams can go down the stairs to the **south-east** of this building, where there is another Hazardous Phantom just to the **south**, which almost doubles the speed (with the risk of having a full spawn on both floors and of being pushed by the fear to the **west**, where there are many monsters).
Second Hazardous Phantom, to the south

It is one of the easiest fights of the quest, but the boss also causes fear. The Knight blocks the boss in the **centre** of the room; the shooters run around to bring the summons ({creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters}, {creature:Weeping Soul|Weeping Souls} and {creature:Spiteful Spitter|Spiteful Spitters}) to the Knight and avoid melee. If there are too many summons, use waves and {item:Great Fireball Rune|Great Fireballs}; the mages attack the boss with spells and {item:Sudden Death Rune|Sudden Deaths}.

Every **14 seconds** a {item:Cleansed Soul Splinter|purple flame} appears on one side of the room. A player steps on it to put it out and then cannot put out another one for **60 seconds** (*"Your soul has recovered!"* tells you when you can). Everyone (including the Knight) takes turns in a **fixed order** agreed before the fight. If nobody steps on it, the boss absorbs it and gets stronger.

When a Weeping Soul dies, its corpse becomes a {item:Pool of Tears}. Whoever steps on it turns into a {creature:Water Elemental} and takes **huge Energy damage** from the boss and the summons. Since it cannot always be avoided, wear Energy protection.

In the recommended order the team already has **2 taints** here: controlling the number of summons in the room makes the difference between failing and succeeding. Some teams place a Fire Bomb in the centre, where the Knight blocks, so that he doesn't run off from the fear (but he is more vulnerable while feared).
Open the boss's corpse: it can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1).
75,000 experience; possible The Skull of a Beast
The wiki does not describe the exit from the boss room: go back the way you came to the Flickering Soul's hub.
Recommended protection: **Holy** and **Energy** (at the boss: **Death** and **Fire**). Attack with **Earth**. {creature:Goshnar's Cruelty} can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1).

In the hub, enter the **fourth Fog Portal** (counting from the left). You arrive at a safe zone. To go down each floor and reach the boss's lever room, each player has to collect **40**, **55** and **70** {item:Pulsating Energy|Pulsating Energies} on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd floors. You can see your progress in the {wiki:Quest Log}.
The energies work like monster blood: hit the creatures until they drop energies on the ground and walk over them.

When you hit a {creature:Cloak of Terror}, a pool of {item:The Blood of Cloak of Terror} appears beneath it: it works like an energy field, but takes much more (up to around **20% of maximum health**, depending on the size of the pool). Cloaks of Terror heal **1,500–2,000 HP** when they walk over their own blood.

Enter the respawn and pull one or two {creature:Vibrant Phantom|Vibrant Phantoms} and/or {creature:Courage Leech|Courage Leeches}. Lay {item:Fire Bomb Rune|Fire Bombs} or {item:Poison Bomb Rune|Poison Bombs} on the ground and make them walk over them: each hit drops several energies. If a Cloak of Terror appears, lead it away or stop running (so you don't spread the blood) and kill it with single-target attacks. When everyone has the energies, move on to the next floor through the fog teleport on the **east** side of the area.

On arrival you immediately have several monsters in front of you (from a little less to more than a full box). Put the melee monsters on the Knight and do **not** use {spell:Chivalrous Challenge} on the Vibrant Phantoms until the Cloaks and most of the Courage Leeches are dead. Then repeat the bomb technique. When everyone has the energies, continue through the fog teleport **next to the entrance** of this floor.

Once again you may have several monsters at the entrance. Repeat the same technique until the whole team has the energies (here the monsters are likely to respawn before you finish). Then enter the lever room through the fog teleport **next to the entrance**.

Experienced teams send the Paladin to jump down first to the 2nd and 3rd floors and draw most of the monsters away from the entrance: the floors are circular, so he can go all the way round or turn back.

It is one of the hardest parts of the quest (in the recommended order the team already has **3 taints**). The longer the fight lasts, the more **resistant** the boss becomes; this cannot be avoided, but it can be delayed considerably with the mechanics. Assign the roles before going in: the Knight stays near the **centre** (the boss can be attacked from all sides) and near the Mean Maw spawn; two shooters (usually the Paladin and the Sorcerer) handle the Poor Souls on the **left** side; the other two stay by the **right** wall or to the **south**, dealing damage and healing.

They spawn in the **south-west** part. A shooter stays near the spawn, pulls the {creature:Poor Soul} and leads it **north**, in front of {creature:A Greedy Eye}. The eye's beam kills it and leaves {item:Some Mortal Essence} on the ground. Careful: the beam also hits you for 3,000 Drown.

Take the Mortal Essence **south** and use it on the {item:Greedy Maw}. When it works, *"The hunger for cruelty has lessened!"* appears. If it sometimes doesn't work, it is because you are doing it faster than the limit allows (a good sign).
**Room explosion** (*"Goshnar's Cruelty begins to channel its energy! Prepare!"*)
Every 60–70 seconds; 6 seconds later the whole room takes up to 3,000 Physical.
Every 30 seconds a random player turns into a {wiki:Massive Fire Elemental} and explodes 6 seconds later (up to 3,500 Fire in a huge area). Whoever is transformed moves away from the others.
It spawns in the south-centre of the room. It is immune to {spell:Challenge}: the Knight can only draw its target by blocking its path while it walks.
Since the {wiki:Avatar} spells were introduced, many teams use them right at the start, when the boss has fewer resistances. Lower-level teams can save them for when there are too many summons.
Open the boss's corpse: it can drop {item:The Skull of a Beast} (addon 1).
75,000 experience; possible The Skull of a Beast
The wiki does not describe the exit from the boss room: go back the way you came to the Flickering Soul's hub.

Recommended protection: **Holy** and **Earth** (at the boss: **Death** and **Fire**). Attack with **Fire**. {creature:Goshnar's Hatred} is the boss that drops the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} (addon 2).
In the hub, enter the **second Fog Portal** (counting from the left). You arrive at a safe zone; once you enter the respawn you are in the main room of the {wiki:Rotten Wasteland}.
The monsters here can root you (*Rooted*): you cannot move for 3 seconds.

To open the boss portal you have to use four shrines, one in each branch, spread over three floors. The paths start from the main room and are direct (see the maps). **Every** team member has to use each shrine. After using a shrine, enter the teleport next to it to return to the centre of the main room (it is not a safe zone, but one is very close). You can see in the {wiki:Quest Log} which ones you have already activated.
With the four shrines activated, go to the far **west** of the main room, go through the door and down the stairs. There you will find the portal to the lever room of {creature:Goshnar's Hatred}.

It is one of the easiest bosses, so it is left for last (with **4 taints**). Keep moving between the two pillars, attacking the boss, the pillars and the {creature:Hateful Soul|Hateful Souls} at the same time with area damage. The shooters stay to the **north** and **south** and leave the middle free for the Knight. Every 8 seconds an *exori*-type spell goes off around each character and deals **Life Drain** to the others: don't stand together.

In the centre of the room there is a fire that grows: {item:Ashes of Burning Hatred} → {item:Spark of Burning Hatred} → {item:Flame of Burning Hatred} → {item:Blaze of Burning Hatred}. The bigger it gets, the stronger the boss. Kill the Hateful Souls and use their corpses ({item:Sorrow}) on the fire whenever you can.

A counter next to your name goes up by 1 every 3 seconds. At **30** you take a strong Death hit every 3 seconds (*"The dread's torment is killing you!"*). To reset it to zero, destroy the {wiki:Symbol of Hatred|Symbols of Hatred} that spawn in the **east** and **west** of the room and step on the remains ({item:Condensed Remorse}). Agree on an order so each of you can reset your counter.
Open the boss's corpse: it can drop the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} (addon 2).
The wiki does not describe the exit from the boss room: go back the way you came to the Flickering Soul's hub.
7. Goshnar's Megalomania and the base outfit

Recommended protection: **Physical** (Stone Skin Amulets, especially the Knight), **Death**, **Energy** and **Fire**. Attack with **Death** on single targets and with **Fire** in area (Great Fireballs and the mages' waves). The wiki's loot list for the final boss does not include the addon items, but it is the boss that gives you the base outfit.

After killing the **five** access bosses, enter the portal to the **south-west** of the hub. The fight combines many of the mechanics of the previous ones and the **5th taint** applies here: your mana drops very quickly and you cannot keep much of it, so don't panic.

Each time you want to kill {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} you have to kill the five access bosses again. The boss has a cooldown of **2 days and 20 hours** (68 h) and the fight lasts at most **20 minutes**.

{creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} changes form during the fight: **purple** — immune to all damage (this is how it starts); **green** ({creature:Goshnar's Megalomania (Vulnerable)}) — vulnerable; **blue** ({creature:Goshnar's Megalomania (Annihilation)}) — prepares the Annihilation attack, but stays vulnerable.
Making it vulnerable with the Aspects of Power

With the boss immune, kill **4 {creature:Aspect of Power|Aspects of Power}**: the boss turns green and vulnerable for **70 seconds**, so deal it all the damage you can. Aspects killed while the boss is vulnerable **do not count** towards the next cycle. The shooters should attack the Aspects with single-target attacks (so as not to spawn more {creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters} because of the 2nd taint) and only use area attacks when there are several Harvesters or when they can hit the boss and the Aspects at the same time.
Dealing with the Splinters of Madness

The boss has an invisible **Madness** counter: it rises over time and with failed mechanics, and the higher it is, the less damage the boss takes. During the fight {wiki:Lesser Splinter of Madness|Lesser Splinters of Madness} spawn, which become {wiki:Greater Splinter of Madness|Greater} and then {wiki:Mighty Splinter of Madness|Mighty}. Lead them over the corpses of the Aspects of Power ({item:Phantasmal Ooze}): they turn into {item:Cleansed Sanity}, which you have to use on the {item:Maw (Object)|Maw} in the **south** of the room (as at Goshnar's Cruelty). If there are several, deal with the strongest one first.
If a Mighty Splinter of Madness is not dealt with in time, the boss absorbs it and the Madness rises.

Two {wiki:Necromantic Focus|Necromantic Focuses} spawn in the **west** and **east** of the room. When killed they leave {item:Necromantic Remains}: stepping on them lowers the Madness (*"Your soul is weakened by the destruction of the remains but the intensity of madness is lessened!"*); if nobody steps on them, the boss absorbs them. The fight can be done while ignoring them: only attack them when the boss is immune and there are no Aspects alive. At the same time, your **Dread's Torment** counter goes up every 10 seconds; at **36** you start taking up to **5,600 Death** every 10 seconds (*"The dread's torment is now lethal!"*), around 700 with SSA, Might Ring and imbuements. Reset it to zero by stepping on a Phantasmal Ooze (you are vulnerable to phantasmal damage for a few seconds).

The oozes are also needed for the Splinters. The best moment for someone to reset their counter is when an Aspect dies and there is no Splinter in the room. Agree on the order beforehand and don't let several players get close to 36.
Besides the main mechanics, you have to deal with these attacks:
It is Life Drain. Normally it is *minor*, but it is *massive* if you stepped on a Phantasmal Ooze shortly before.
Every 30 seconds, an *exori*-type spell around each character deals Life Drain to the other players: don't stand together.
A random player is transformed and explodes 6 seconds later (Fire damage over a large area): move away from the others.

{item:White Stone Tile|White tiles} appear and destroy the Necromantic Remains on the ground; 8 seconds later anyone who is **not** on a tile takes **10,000 Death**. It only happens 2 or 3 times: decide beforehand who steps on the tiles and who takes the hit with SSA, Might Ring and Death protection.
The boss turns blue, roots itself in place and shouts *"NOW - I - WILL - ANNIHILATE - YOU!"*. Move away from it but keep attacking. It only happens once and lasts about 7 seconds.
The boss can cause fear (*Feared*) on its target.

Strong teams use the {wiki:Avatar} spells in the first green phase: the boss turns blue when its health gets to just above yellow, and if that happens in the first rotation of Aspects a lot of time is saved. Weaker teams need more rotations.
Reporting to the Flickering Soul and receiving the base outfit
After defeating the boss, go back to the hub and talk to the {npc:Flickering Soul}: {key:hi} and {key:task}. You receive the base **Revenant Outfits** (male and female).
Official artwork of the Revenant Outfits

Enter the portal **behind** a {npc:Flickering Soul} in the main room and open the {item:Brass-Shod Chest} to the **north**. It gives **one** random item from the {wiki:Soul Set|Soul Set}, only once per character.
A random item from the Soul Set

In the chest room, the {item:Magic Forcefield} takes you straight to the **Thais depot**. If you have not reached this room yet (for example, after hunting only the access bosses), the wiki describes no other exit: go back the way you came in to the Vengoth teleport ({coord:32962,31497,7}), walk **south-west** to {npc:Harlow} and say {key:hi}, {key:yalahar}, {key:yes} (50 gp). In Yalahar, if you have already done the *Searoutes around Yalahar* mission of the {wiki:In Service of Yalahar Quest|In Service of Yalahar Quest}, {npc:Karith} (at the harbour, on a ship 1 floor up) takes you to your city ({key:hi}, city name, {key:yes}; see table). If not, {npc:Captain Cookie}, on the ship to the left of Karith's, takes you to **Liberty Bay** (400 gp) or **Thais** (800 gp).
8. First addon: The Skull of a Beast
{item:The Skull of a Beast} (*"Unleash the beast."*, 2.30 oz) gives the first addon. It drops from four of the Soul War access bosses, or you can buy it on the Market.
Quick option: buy on the Market
Search for **The Skull of a Beast** on the Market at any depot and buy it. No NPC sells it. If you buy it, skip to the step "Use The Skull of a Beast".
The price is negotiated between players; compare the offers before buying.
Hunt the item from the bosses
If you prefer to hunt it, kill the bosses that drop it (sections 2 to 5). Each one has a **20-hour** cooldown, and the wiki's rates come from small samples, so expect several attempts.
Use The Skull of a Beast
Use {item:The Skull of a Beast} (right-click → *Use*). You receive the **first addon** of the Revenant Outfits and the message *"Now the beast is unleashed!"*.
The {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} (1.50 oz) gives the second addon. It drops from Goshnar's Hatred, or you can buy it on the Market.
Quick option: buy on the Market
Search for **Bracelet of Strengthening** on the Market and buy it. No NPC sells it. If you buy it, skip to the step "Use the Bracelet of Strengthening".
Hunt the item from Goshnar's Hatred

Kill {creature:Goshnar's Hatred} in the Rotten Wasteland (section 6), with a **20-hour** cooldown between attempts (the wiki does not give the rate: only 12 kills recorded). The wiki's loot statistics also record a Bracelet of Strengthening from {creature:Goshnar's Malice} (section 2), in a sample of only 17 kills.

Use the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} (right-click → *Use*). You receive the **second addon** and the message *"Wild power flows though your body!"*. Once you have used both items ({item:The Skull of a Beast} and the Bracelet of Strengthening), you earn the achievement **Unleash the Beast**.
Revenant Outfits addon 2 and the Unleash the Beast achievement (with both addons)

Summary: **base outfit** from the {wiki:Soul War Quest|Soul War Quest} (defeat {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} and report to the {npc:Flickering Soul}); **addon 1** with {item:The Skull of a Beast} (dropped by Goshnar's Malice, Greed, Spite or Cruelty); **addon 2** with the {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} (dropped by Goshnar's Hatred). Both items can be bought and sold on the Market.

The wiki is inconsistent about the numbering: the quest spoiler says The Skull of a Beast gives the **first** addon and the Bracelet the **second**, but the item pages say the opposite. To get the full outfit and the achievement you always need both.

Achievement **Unleash the Beast** (8 points): *"You defeated the manifestation of Goshnar's evil traits by fighting your way through beasts you didn't even want to imagine. It transformed you and now you can also look the part."*

If the team fails the fight with Goshnar's Megalomania, each player loses their **last two** taints and the progress of **two random bosses** (the same for the whole team); you can see which ones by saying {key:shards} to the Flickering Soul. Defeating the final boss clears the taints.
Having taints increases the chance of Soul War monsters and bosses dropping a {item:Bag You Desire}.
The Soul War Quest can also give the achievement **Soul Mender** (under certain conditions), as well as the Soul Set item.
